The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made certain things unlawful for himself, though he had not made them unlawful for the people.

Here Allah, glorified is He, clarifies this for him: "Do not make unlawful for yourself what Allah has made lawful for you." So this is a matter for the Messenger's own benefit. The determination of what is forbidden (tahrim) and what is permitted (tahlil) is entrusted to the Creator, glorified is He, and it is never for a human being to interfere in this. A person's interference sometimes takes the form of forbidding what Allah has made lawful, and sometimes the form of making lawful what Allah has forbidden. Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 87].

As for the verse ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾, it points to a matter that angered the Prophet (ﷺ), so that he abstained from some things that the human soul desires, things which Allah had made lawful.

The Prophet did not make lawful what Allah had forbidden; rather, he made unlawful for himself what Allah had made lawful for him. This runs against his own interest, and it is as though Allah, glorified is He, is asking him: "Why do you burden yourself?" So this is a rebuke for the benefit of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Prohibition is a constraint upon the self, and Allah, glorified is He, rebukes His Messenger because he constrained himself and made unlawful for himself what Allah had made lawful for him, just as you rebuke your son who stayed up studying for a long time until he exhausted himself. The rebuke is for the Prophet's benefit, not against it.

Allah, exalted is He, made some things lawful and some things unlawful, so do not shift anything from what is unlawful to what is lawful, nor anything from what is lawful to what is unlawful, as the Creator, glorified is He, said: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ [al-A'raf: 32].

Your Lord, O Muhammad, does not constrain you, and He forbids you to constrain yourself and make unlawful for yourself what He has made lawful for you, just as He blames you for making lawful what He has made unlawful for you, because that is for your good.
